newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index reverses decline, ends up 74.56.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index reverses decline, ends up 74.56.

text.p: Most Hungarian share prices consolidated on Wedenesday as the Hungarian BUX Index reversed recent declines, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 3,565.00, up 74.56 points.
The rise was led by oil and gas company MOL which closed at 1,720 forints, up 65, and pharmaceuticals maker Richter, which ended 250 higher at 8,200.
MOL's large rise surprised many traders as they had expected it to continue Tuesday's fall ahead of an expected government announcement tomorrow of energy price rises.
Reports have predicted that gas, for which MOL is the exclusive supplier, will rise by 16 percent, a figure which Nomura described to Reuters this week as "totally inadequate".
"It seems the market believes tomorrow's rises will be enough to make a profit," said Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities.
"It seems incredible to me because they need a rise of 16 to 20 percent and even 16 percent for the consumer could only mean 10 percent for MOL."

Adam Santha of Daiwa-MKB said he believed the recent confidence in chemicals manufacturer TVK, which rose 45 to end at 1,380 forints, could have had a psychological effect, pushing up prices elsewhere.
Santha added that traders had ignored Nomura's concerns.
"I believe Nomura was wrong to worry so much about the energy price rise. I think the decision could be better than expected," he said.
Both dealers said the other big gainer, Richter, was less surprising.
"Richter has good markets throughout the region and investors realise it is undervalued," said Agoston.
Santha said that Richter was now at a similar level to its competitor Egis.
"At one point, Egis was 1,000 forints higher. As both companies are roughly equivalent this was definitely too much of a difference," Santha said.
All BUX index futures ended higher by 20 to 50 points.
